title: What If We Cleaned Up the Great Pacific Garbage Patch?

scenes.text: What if we cleaned up the Great Pacific Garbage Patch? The hard part isn't the size.
It covers about 1.6 million square kilometers, and holds roughly 80,000 tonnes of plastic, as heavy as 500 jumbo jets.
A cleanup system called Jenny has pulled out about 101 tonnes in 45 hauls. That is a tiny fraction of the total.
Cleaning all of it would take roughly a thousand hauls of 100 tonnes each, and the nets keep running.
Worse, scientists estimate 1.8 trillion pieces, and most are smaller than half a centimeter. Nets can't catch them.
So the real fix isn't at sea. Turn off the tap on land first, or the ocean refills the patch.
